clue.text: Disenchanted princess's fantasy: to get prince, in short!

blocks.note: DI is the usual short form for a princess, with the possessive 's kept on
a fantasy is a false belief or illusion
Ed is the short form of Edward, a royal prince's name

explanation.surface: A disenchanted princess dreams of landing a prince, quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a crossword staple for princess, from Princess Diana; the possessive gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disillusioned has lost their ideals and faith, which is exactly what being disenchanted means: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Single male (brother) and heartless girl in endless love tangle

indicators.note: without a heart, the middle of the word is taken out
without an end, the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for male
bro is informal for brother
girl with its two middle letters removed
in with its last letter cut off
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A bachelor, his brother and a cold-hearted girl caught up in a messy love triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love tangle' reads as one phrase, but love is the O and only 'tangle' defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, complicated situation or misunderstanding, a figurative synonym for a tangle.

clue.text: Picture Arachne's senility!

blocks.note: Arachne is the setter, so 'Arachne is' becomes I'M
senility comes with old age

explanation.surface: The setter jokingly displays her own decline into old age.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themselves means I or ME; here the 's stands for 'is', giving I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a visual representation such as a painting or photograph, a straightforward synonym for a picture.

clue.text: In feudal times, a sovereign city in Europe

blocks.note: first meaning: a feudal lord owed allegiance by vassals
second meaning: Liège, a city in eastern Belgium

explanation.surface: A history note about a medieval monarch ruling over a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: Liège is spelt with an accent in Belgium, but crosswords ignore accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Under feudalism a liege was the superior lord to whom vassals swore loyalty and service, and Liège is a Belgian city.

clue.text: Civil servant closed a railway

blocks.note: closed, as in private or hidden from others
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A government official shuts down a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior civil servant heading a department is a Permanent Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretary can be a government official or administrative officer, so the word fits a civil servant.

clue.text: Half legless drunk ogled Gene

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering and disordered, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy person leers at a man called Gene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, which fits the surface; here it is read literally, with half the legs gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing half your legs leaves you with just one, a witty literal reading of a word normally meaning extremely intoxicated.

clue.text: The King lives? Dubious!

indicators.note: something dubious is doubtful or unsound, hinting the letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sceptical response to the rumour that the King of rock and roll is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to the long-running 'Elvis is alive' rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's nickname was the King of Rock and Roll, often shortened to simply the King.

clue.text: Girl gets very little money for old bicycle

blocks.note: Penny is a girl's name
a farthing was a quarter of an old penny, the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A girl is paid a pittance for selling her antique bike.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The penny-farthing was a Victorian high-wheeled bicycle with one huge front wheel and a tiny rear one.

clue.text: In a bad temper, aims for misunderstandings

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
aims are intentions or purposes

explanation.surface: Someone angry sets goals that lead to confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: When people are at cross purposes they misunderstand each other, each pursuing a different idea of the conversation.

clue.text: After end of affaire, married couple hug each other

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, and that letter is the one kept

blocks.note: the final letter of affaire
M is the abbreviation for married
a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Once their fling is over, the husband and wife make up with a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace is for two people to clasp each other closely in their arms, the same act as a mutual hug.

clue.text: Chopper about to take off, right?

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to take off is to depart
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A helicopter pilot checks it is ready to lift off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' and 'take off' paint a helicopter, but the chopper is a butcher's knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy broad-bladed knife used by butchers for hacking through meat and bone.

clue.text: Love to be in front end of plane for loop

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the nose is the forward end of an aircraft
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A romance blossoming in the front of an aircraft, as it performs a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: Teams initially expecting some light refreshment

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the words that follow it

blocks.note: football and cricket teams have eleven players, so a team is an eleven
the first letter of expecting
the first letter of some

explanation.surface: Sports teams look forward to a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, taken around eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a small snack and drink taken in the late morning, which is a light refreshment.

clue.text: Planes and trains

blocks.note: first meaning: smooths wood with a tool, as with a rasp
second meaning: lines of people or things one behind another

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests transport; planes are tools for smoothing and trains are queues.
explanation.definitionFit: To file is to smooth with an abrasive tool, as planing does, and files are rows or processions, like trains.

clue.text: Sorted car out? It gets one credit

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets their car fixed and buys it on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted' looks like part of the indicator, but its letters are fodder along with car; 'out' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A store card is a shop's own credit card, which lets the holder buy goods on credit.

clue.text: Butterfly, bats, pigeon, rat

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of creatures: a butterfly, bats, a pigeon and a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: In the list 'bats' poses as another animal, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a common European butterfly whose males have bright orange wingtips: an example of the category.

clue.text: Stubborn, awkward beast? Not I!

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and ill-arranged, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone accused of being a difficult, mulish creature denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate describes a person who refuses to change their mind or course, a direct synonym for stubborn.

clue.text: Boy finally came on board on schedule

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word it goes with

blocks.note: Tim is a boy's name
the last letter of came
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A boy at last joined the company, right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'on' just places the pieces in order; the second is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable is a list of times at which events such as trains or classes happen, a synonym for schedule.

clue.text: I lost your cocktail; it's how revellers behave!

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A party guest apologises for losing someone's drink amid the merriment.
explanation.definitionFit: Partygoers who are carousing act in a wild, noisy, unrestrained manner, the adverb describing such behaviour.

clue.text: Object is almost prudish

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: demure means modest or prim

explanation.surface: A thing is described as nearly prim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb, to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise doubts or show reluctance, the verb sense of object as to protest.

clue.text: Girl embraced by this eccentric Greek scholar

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or unconventional, so the letters go out of their usual order
something embraced is held inside another's arms, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then reordered
Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is hugged by an oddball classicist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellenist is a specialist in the language and culture of ancient Greece, so a scholar of Greek.

clue.text: Australian arboriculturist shelters tropical plant

indicators.note: to shelter is to hold within, so the letters sit inside the words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A tree expert from Australia protects a jungle plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine that hangs from trees in tropical rainforests.

clue.text: First of toddlers runs onto play area

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, kept here

blocks.note: the opening letter of toddlers
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
to act is to perform or play a part

explanation.surface: The first little one dashes into the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play area' reads as a playground, but play gives letters and only 'area' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a large stretch of land or expanse, so it means an area.

clue.text: Morse's short note to the above

blocks.note: in spoken Morse code the short signal, the dot, is called dit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse jots a brief memo referring to what was written earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse here is the code, not the TV detective; dit and dah are the short and long signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same as what was written previously, used in lists to repeat the item written above.

clue.text: Government ministry fared badly

indicators.note: done badly means wrongly put together, so the letters need reordering

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A government department did poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: DEFRA is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: DEFRA is the acronym of a British government department, so it is an example of a ministry.

clue.text: Return again to river, a river in North America

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
R is the abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to a river again.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'river' gives a single letter; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara is the river flowing between Lakes Erie and Ontario on the US–Canada border, famous for its falls.

clue.text: A fine female, clever and good-natured

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
F is the abbreviation for female
able means capable or skilled

explanation.surface: A description of an admirable woman: smart and kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly and easy to talk to, which is what good-natured means.

clue.text: Boat on River Dart pleased me terribly

indicators.note: terribly means very badly, so the letters are put into a jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trip on a boat along the Devon river was a huge delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a river in Devon, England, but here it is just letters for the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a steam-powered vessel driven by paddle wheels, typically used on rivers and lakes.
